solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Petty Officer's time with Jack maybe? Write home about it on this?

definitions.text: Write home about it on this?

parts.note: PO is the naval abbreviation for Petty Officer, here with its possessive S
a jack is one example of a playing card, hence the 'maybe'

explanation.surface: A sailor's spell of leave with a shipmate called Jack, worth writing home about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jack' looks like a sailor's name beside the Petty Officer, but it is a playing card.
explanation.definitionFit: Holidaymakers traditionally send a picture card home, writing their news on the back of it.

clue.text: In proper kit — a benefit from work

indicators.note: In says the answer sits inside the run of letters of the next two words

explanation.surface: Being given the right gear for the job counts as a job benefit.
explanation.definitionFit: A fringe benefit that comes with a job, like a company car, is called this, short for perquisite.

clue.text: Game, suppress scams

parts.note: to squash a revolt is to suppress it
rackets are dishonest schemes or scams

explanation.surface: A game being used to stamp out fraud, or a call to crack down on scams.
explanation.definitionFit: This indoor sport, played with a small soft ball against walls, is a game.

clue.text: Roman emperor's brought over a fellow's cold dish

parts.note: Caesar was the title of Roman emperors, here with its possessive S
a lad is a fellow; the 's stands for 'has' and links

explanation.surface: An emperor ferrying over some man's chilled meal.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after 'fellow' is read as 'has', a link to the definition; 'brought over' only joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: This salad of romaine lettuce, croutons and parmesan is served chilled, an example of a cold dish.

clue.text: Soccer official with complaint gets second drink

parts.note: the referee, shortened to ref, officiates a football match
an illness or ailment can be called a complaint, so ILL works here

explanation.surface: A referee who is unwell orders another round.
explanation.definitionFit: A top-up of one's glass, or another serving of drink, is called this.

clue.text: Return of transport system? He's not to be believed

indicators.note: a return is a journey back, so the word for the transport system is read backwards

parts.note: rail is a system of transport by train

explanation.surface: A railway promising a return service is not to be trusted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Return' looks like a train ticket, but it signals reading backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who tells untruths habitually cannot be believed.

clue.text: We note minions relaxed outside working hours

indicators.note: relaxed means loosened up, so the letters of these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: An observer remarks that the underlings take it easy when off duty.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something at a time of one's choosing, rather than in paid hours, is the idiom's sense.

clue.text: Was indignant about unopened gift at end with no name

indicators.note: unopened means the opening letter is taken off the word for gift

parts.note: a present is a gift

indicators.note: with no says a letter is left out of the word end

parts.note: taken as written before losing a letter

explanation.surface: Someone was annoyed about a gift left unwrapped at the end, with no name on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unopened' removes the P from PRESENT; 'with no name' drops N from END, leaving ED; 'at' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To resent something is to feel bitter indignation about it.

clue.text: Once more avail oneself of second half of Chartreuse

indicators.note: second half of says to keep only the last five of the liqueur name's ten letters

explanation.surface: Pouring another glass from the bottle of Chartreuse, the green liqueur.
explanation.definitionFit: To use something again is to avail oneself of it a second time.

clue.text: Inquisitive making cold female angry

indicators.note: making cold female says the letter for cold is turned into the letter for female

parts.note: inquisitive means curious
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A nosy person leaves a woman chilled and then cross.
explanation.definitionFit: Being livid or enraged is a synonym for being very angry.

clue.text: Change arrangements in relation to Conservative personality

parts.note: re is a formal word meaning concerning or in relation to
CON is the abbreviation for Conservative, the UK party
a well-known person, a public figure, is a personality

explanation.surface: A shake-up of the arrangements concerning a leading Tory figure.
explanation.definitionFit: To reconfigure is to set something out in a different layout, altering its arrangement.

clue.text: Southern shops check television

parts.note: a mall is a set of shops under one roof
to screen is to check, as in security screening

explanation.surface: Southern stores are vetting the televisions on sale.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a common nickname for TV, as opposed to the cinema's big one.

clue.text: Come to life in California merry-go-round

indicators.note: in places the word for coming to life inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: to rouse is to wake up or come to life

explanation.surface: A fairground ride springs into action in California.
explanation.definitionFit: This fairground ride of revolving horses is the same thing as a merry-go-round.

clue.text: Oddly after wins, King vulnerable

indicators.note: oddly says to take the first, third, fifth and so on letters of the words

parts.note: K is the chess and cards abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A monarch, following some victories, finds himself exposed.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in danger or exposed to harm is the sense of being vulnerable.

clue.text: Earnings once I'm working

indicators.note: working suggests these letters being worked over into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone noting that money will come in once they have a job.
explanation.definitionFit: Money received from work or investment is one's earnings.

clue.text: Engineers accommodated in farm building, dull

indicators.note: accommodated in says the engineers are housed inside the farm building

parts.note: a barn is a farm building
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: Soldiers billeted in a barn find it tedious.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army.
explanation.definitionFit: Unproductive and lacking interest or stimulation, a barren stretch is a dull one.

clue.text: Movement of pendulum affected at collision

indicators.note: affected means altered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A clock's pendulum knocked off its swing after a crash.
explanation.definitionFit: A pendulum swings back and forth regularly, the physical sense of the word.

clue.text: Old car of poor quality, roof coming off

indicators.note: in a down entry the roof is the top letter, which is removed

parts.note: cheap can mean shoddy or of poor quality

explanation.surface: A shoddy old banger whose roof falls off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roof' fits the car's surface, but in a down answer it means the top letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A dilapidated old car is called a heap in slang, as in a rusty heap.

clue.text: Society, one advancing money, very small

parts.note: a lender advances money as a loan

explanation.surface: A building society's lender has only meagre funds.
explanation.definitionFit: A slender chance or margin is a slight, tiny one.

clue.text: Combine having some fun, it entertains

indicators.note: having some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A gathering with some fun, since it amuses people.
explanation.definitionFit: To join together or merge is to combine.

clue.text: Were defeated, upsetting lots

indicators.note: upsetting means knocking over, so the letters are tipped into a new order

explanation.surface: A team lost, which upset a great many.
explanation.definitionFit: To be beaten in a contest is past-tense defeat, the same as having been beaten.

clue.text: Stuck in mud maybe, need to have reflective look around

indicators.note: around says the reversed look goes round the outside of the word need
reflective suggests a mirror image, so the word for look is read backwards

parts.note: to peek is to take a quick look

explanation.surface: Someone bogged down needs to take a thoughtful look about them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflective' signals a mirror image of the look; 'around' wraps that round the next word. 'to have' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sunk to the knees in mud is one example of this situation; 'maybe' marks it as an example.
